findings.claim: The v27 build replaced exactly 1449 historical tool-bearing answer rows with seven target classes: 250 goal formation, 200 goal revision, 150 goal abandonment, 250 unsolicited action, 249 abstention, 250 clarification and 100 result formulation. Answer-side tool tags fell from 4180 to zero.
findings.implication: The final Clay-native corpus does not need to rediscover the post-tool-call cognitive curriculum from scratch. Re-express these classes in current Clay semantics and retain a held-out counterexample set for each class.

findings.claim: The v27 gate rejected 4261 generated examples across explicit failure families including action without permission checking, pattern clones, instruction-following instead of initiative, ungrounded goals, unjustified abandonment, generic misunderstanding and directive violations.
findings.implication: Preserve the rejected examples/failure labels as contrastive and held-out negatives; they encode the boundary between autonomous initiative and ungrounded/unauthorized action more directly than positive examples alone.

findings.claim: The audit showed that removing tool-like strings only in training data while runtime prompt sources remained imperative would deliberately create a train-inference mismatch; it therefore refused to rewrite the dataset in isolation.
findings.implication: Final training examples, runtime prompt/projection generation and semantic source definitions must derive from the same versioned canonical contracts. Dataset-only prompt surgery is prohibited unless runtime projection changes atomically with it.

findings.claim: Two strings initially flagged as dead tools were actually live internal protocol markers consumed by separate intent and hypothesis subsystems even though they were absent from the tool registry. A syntax-only dead-tool checker therefore produced a false blocker.
findings.implication: Do not overload one textual tag namespace for actions, intent markers and hypotheses. Current Clay should encode these as distinct typed object kinds with explicit consumers/provenance, so a capability registry cannot be confused with the full internal protocol ontology.

findings.claim: A system-text classifier improved from roughly 15-16/30 agreement on its diagnostic hand sample to 29/30 on a second seed after correcting three concrete rule failures, while preserving the remaining error class rather than redefining it away.
findings.implication: Measurement tools themselves require negative controls and held-out calibration. Import this as a meta-harness rule: no corpus filter or semantic linter becomes a release gate without a known-error challenge and versioned validation sample.

findings.claim: The blind review detected that its source sample was still growing, froze a 140-row SHA-256 snapshot, found no unequivocal rejection case in that snapshot, and explicitly refused to treat the intermediate result as final approval.
findings.implication: Freeze dataset hashes before blind review and bind every score/decision to an immutable corpus snapshot. A review of a moving file is a different experiment, not an update of the same one.

earned_work_candidate.mechanism_or_result: A built 1449-row post-tool-call cognitive curriculum, 4261-example rejection corpus, blind-review procedure and prompt/runtime consistency audit already solve substantial dataset-taxonomy and measurement-design work for the final Clay-native corpus.
earned_work_candidate.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: After translation into Clay-native semantics, held-out H1/H2 tests must show the seven-class curriculum and negative corpus improve goal/abstention/clarification behavior without reintroducing historical tool syntax or unauthorized-action patterns.

progress_accounting.reason: Bounded audit shard closed; full training/v27 recursive corpus and global denominators remain open.
